original_question: Which polytopes P have the property that their monodromy group Mon(P) is a string C-group?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1: whether every convex polytope with combinatorially regular facets, possibly of more than one facet type, has monodromy group Mon(P) a string C-group.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s central object, the monodromy group Mon(P), and the precise group-theoretic property under discussion, namely being a string C-group.
missing_details: The paper does not ask for a classification of all polytopes P with this property; it asks a universal yes/no conjecture.
The conjecture is restricted to convex polytopes with combinatorially regular facets.
The facets are allowed to come in different regular types; the point is not equifacettedness.
To be stand-alone, the question should specify that Mon(P) is the flag-adjacency-generated monodromy group of P.
The nearby context links this question to minimal regular covers: Proposition 1.2 gives the paper’s equivalent reformulation in terms of uniqueness of the minimal regular cover.
Theorem 1.3 shows the conjecture for the specific family of fully truncated simplices, so the paper’s main theorem is evidence for the conjecture rather than a classification of all such polytopes.
refined_question: Let P be a convex polytope whose facets are combinatorially regular polytopes, not necessarily all of the same type, and let Mon(P) be the monodromy group generated by the involutions sending each flag of P to its i-adjacent flag. Must Mon(P) always be a string C-group (equivalently, with respect to these standard generators, must it satisfy the string commuting relations and the intersection property)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does every convex polytope with combinatorially regular facets have a unique minimal regular cover?
justification: The draft is too broad for this paper. In the introduction, the paper isolates not a full classification problem for arbitrary polytopes, but the narrower conjecture that every convex polytope with combinatorially regular facets has monodromy group a string C-group. Proposition 1.2 supplies the equivalent formulation in terms of uniqueness of the minimal regular cover, and Theorem 1.3 then provides the paper’s main positive result by proving this for fully truncated simplices. So the closest paper-faithful sharpening of the draft is the conjecture with the regular-facet and convexity hypotheses made explicit, not an unrestricted classification question.
